Una massa ovale o rotonda a margini circ:
An oval or round mass with circumscribed margins, without suspicious calcifications, is more often benign (fibroadenoma, cyst, intramammary lymph node). The margins, however, must be described honestly: if part of them is obscured by overlapping tissue, you cannot say “entirely circumscribed”.
On mammography, a new uncharacterized mass is classified BI-RADS 0 and completed with targeted ultrasound: if it is a simple cyst it becomes BI-RADS 2; if it is solid, oval, parallel to the skin and circumscribed it may be BI-RADS 3 (6-month follow-up) or, at age 51, biopsy is often chosen (BI-RADS 4A). Category 5 is reserved for findings with clear signs of malignancy (spiculation, irregular shape, suspicious calcifications).
The small coarse calcification near the mass has a benign appearance and does not change the conclusion.
Outcome from the collection: lesion benign at biopsy (the histotype is not indicated; the most frequent for such a mass is fibroadenoma).
